9.t: Working with data: sap flow over a day
q: Describe the pattern of sap speed at the top of the trunk.
Low at night (2 cm h⁻¹), rising from about 06:00 to a peak at noon (40 cm h⁻¹), then falling in the evening.
Estimate how far sap moves at the top of the trunk between 12:00 and 14:00.
Mean speed about 39 cm h⁻¹ × 2 h = about 78 cm.
Sap speed at the base rises and peaks about 2 hours later than at the top. Explain what this shows about how sap is moved.

The water is pulled from above: transpiration in the leaves creates tension in the xylem first near the top, and this pull is passed down the water column by cohesion. If roots pushed the sap, the base would move first.
Explain why sap still moves slowly at night.
The trunk is refilling with water lost during the day, a little transpiration continues, and there may be some root pressure.
Predict how the curves would differ on a cloudy, humid day.
Lower peaks (less transpiration) and a smaller delay.
